name: Ghost Bulimulus
description:
The Ghost Bulimulus (*Bulimulus bonariensis*), also called the ghost snail or peanut snail, is a small terrestrial gastropod in the family Bulimulidae. Its slender, cone-shaped shell is typically light brown to tan, and adults are usually about ½–1 inch long. Native to South America, this species is introduced in Florida, where it may occur in large aggregations on vegetation, walls, fences, irrigation equipment, and other surfaces.

This 3D model provides an interactive view of its shell shape, whorls, and overall morphology for species identification and biology education.

A 3D model of an Anhinga (*Anhinga anhinga*), a distinctive waterbird commonly found throughout Florida. Often called the “snakebird” because of its long, slender neck, the Anhinga swims with much of its body submerged while the head and neck remain above the water.

Anhingas are highly adapted for aquatic hunting. They pursue fish underwater and use their long, pointed bill to capture prey. Unlike many other waterbirds, their feathers are not completely waterproof, so they are frequently seen perched with their wings spread to dry after swimming.

This interactive model is useful for studying avian anatomy, aquatic adaptations, feeding ecology, plumage, body proportions, and Florida wetland biodiversity.

This compact member of the family Columbidae is found across the southern United States, including Florida, where it commonly inhabits open fields, scrub, coastal dunes, woodland edges, neighborhoods, and other areas with exposed ground and nearby cover.

Common Ground Doves are primarily ground foragers that feed on seeds and grains. Their sandy-brown plumage, dark wing spots, short tail, and subtle scaling on the breast help distinguish them from larger doves. When flushed, the wings can reveal rich reddish-brown coloration.

This interactive model is useful for studying avian anatomy, bird identification, morphology, camouflage, feeding adaptations, and Florida biodiversity.

name: Domestic Chicken
description:
An interactive 3D model of a domestic chicken (Gallus gallus domesticus), presented as an educational specimen for studying avian anatomy, morphology, and external features.

The model allows viewers to examine the chicken from all angles, including the head, beak, comb, wattles, wings, plumage, legs, feet, and overall body proportions. Chickens are members of the family Phasianidae and are domesticated descendants of wild junglefowl.

This model includes two embedded animations: a subtle Idle motion that gives the bird a more natural, lifelike presence, and a 360° Turntable animation for viewing the specimen from all sides.

Useful for biology, zoology, comparative anatomy, animal science, ornithology, vertebrate studies, and 3D science education.

name: Great Blue Heron
description:
A 3D model of a Great Blue Heron (*Ardea herodias*), one of the largest and most recognizable wading birds in North America. Great Blue Herons are common throughout Florida and are frequently found along marshes, estuaries, mangrove shorelines, ponds, canals, and other shallow-water habitats.

Their long legs allow them to wade slowly through shallow water, while the long, pointed bill is adapted for capturing fish, amphibians, crustaceans, and other aquatic prey. Great Blue Herons often remain motionless while hunting before striking rapidly with the bill.

This interactive model allows viewers to examine the heron's elongated neck, spear-like bill, long legs and toes, body proportions, plumage, and characteristic wading-bird anatomy. It is useful for studying bird identification, structure and function, wetland ecology, and adaptations to aquatic environments.

name: Brown Pelican on Channel Marker
description:
A 3D model of a Brown Pelican (*Pelecanus occidentalis*) perched on a marine channel marker post above the water. Brown Pelicans are large coastal seabirds commonly seen throughout Florida, where they inhabit beaches, bays, estuaries, mangrove shorelines, and other coastal environments.

Unlike most pelicans, Brown Pelicans typically capture fish by plunge-diving from the air, using their long bill and expandable throat pouch to scoop prey from the water. Their webbed feet are adapted for swimming, while docks, pilings, channel markers, and other structures provide convenient resting and observation sites.

This model allows viewers to examine the pelican's distinctive bill and throat pouch, webbed feet, body proportions, plumage, and characteristic posture while perched on a structure typical of Florida's coastal waterways.

name: Willet — Coastal Shorebird
description:
The Willet (*Tringa semipalmata*) is a relatively large member of the sandpiper family and a familiar shorebird along Florida's coast.

Willets are generally gray above and white below, although breeding birds develop more extensive brown-gray mottling and speckling. Their long, straight bill is well suited for probing wet sand, shallow water, and mud for prey. The legs are typically blue-gray.

One of the Willet's most recognizable characteristics becomes visible when the bird takes flight. Its wings display a bold black-and-white pattern, with a conspicuous white stripe contrasting strongly against darker portions of the wing. This pattern can make a flying Willet much easier to identify than a resting bird.

name: Ibex horns
description:
Ibex horns are one of the most distinctive features of these animals, growing continuously throughout their lives and curving elegantly backward from the skull. They are composed of a solid bony core covered by a thick layer of keratin, which gives them both strength and resilience. Along their surface, visible ridges or rings often form, marking periods of growth and making each horn unique. In males, the horns can reach impressive lengths and are significantly larger than those of females, playing an important role in social behavior and competition. During mating season, they are used in dramatic clashes where individuals strike each other with force, relying on the horns’ structure to absorb impact. Beyond their functional role, ibex horns contribute to the animal’s iconic silhouette, symbolizing adaptation to harsh, mountainous environments.

This 3D model was realized by Clarissa Bignoli and Erika Del Bene during the Universal Civil Service (SCU) at UniGe.

name: Anomalocaris - Low-Poly & Game-Ready 3D Asset
description:
A low-poly and game-ready Anomalocaris 3D asset that I modelled, textured, rigged, & animated in one day during a 48-hour game jam. 

The now extinct Anomalocaris was one of Earth's first ever apex predators. It was apart of the Radiodonta order, and first appeared during the Cambrian Period around like 500 million years ago :3

------

**Cambrian Carnage**
The game was a co-op arcade survival game where 2 players defend a central tesla tower thingy from these Cambrian-era creatures.

**Texturing**
This asset was my first time experimenting with a gradient atlas texturing workflow *(inspired by Vicente Moscardó Ribes)*  which uses a single 64×64 color pallete texture for all of the assets in the game, which gave a highly optimized, and stylized result! Highly reccomend you try it out.

**Rigging/Animation**
I used Blender’s damped track bone constraint on the bones to make the smooth & dynamic motion, which made it very simple & straight forward to animate. Animations were then baked and exported for Unity.

name: Löwe
description:
The stone lion on Josef-Hyrtl-Platz in Mödling is part of the historic complex of the former Hyrtl Orphanage. The figure dates from around the turn of the century and was erected in front of the orphanage church as a representative decorative element. With its powerful stance, the lion symbolizes strength, protection, and dignity, thus reflecting the social significance of the former institution for poor and orphaned children.

The stone lion continues to shape the appearance of the square to this day and is one of the most famous historical figures in Mödling. For many decades, the sculpture was exposed to the elements, which is why it was restored along with the other lion figures. The restoration was carried out in collaboration with the Federal Monuments Office to preserve these art-historically valuable figures for the long term.

description:
YPM VP.004192 is a fossil tooth of Tyrannosaurus rex and represents the first T. rex tooth ever discovered. The specimen was collected in 1874 from Upper Cretaceous deposits of Jefferson County, Colorado, USA. It belongs to the theropod dinosaur T. rex, one of the largest terrestrial predators of the Late Cretaceous, within the clade Tyrannosauridae.

This high-resolution 3D model was created by the Yale Peabody Museum using 1,340 photographs captured with the COPIS imaging system and reconstructed through Agisoft MetaShape Professional. Original specimen catalog number: YPM VP.004192.

description:
Quad mesh, 1000 vertices, Basecolor, roughness, normal map, metallic, transmission, 30 fps animation, 360 frames, Made in Blender and Substance Painter.


Symphysodon aequifasciatus

The blue discus, or discus fish, is a tropical fish native to South America and is one of the few freshwater species with a disc-shaped body.

They measure between 15 and 20 cm in length and can live up to an average of 12 years.

Their main threats include sudden changes in water conditions, bacterial or parasitic infections caused by poor water quality, and stress resulting from transport or aggression. These factors can lead to loss of coloration and disease.

Their conservation status is classified as Least Concern (LC) according to the IUCN.

name: Chimaera Plumibathypus.
description:
This is my Chimaera creature consisting of the following animals: The Giant Isopod, Flying Fox and the Plumed Basilisk.
The creatures full Scientific (made up) name is "Plumifronobathynomopus," which can be shortened to Plumibathypus.
The Plumibathypus inhabits the Temporate Forest's and lives near rivers. It uses its almost moustache like looking antennae to feel around when swimming, since its eyesight is quite poor in the deeper waters, even though it's an excellent swimmer. It also uses it's antennae and it's large tail when intimidating other creatures to make sure he appears fearsomely even though it feeds solely on dead animals and smaller fish. Another interesting aspect of the creature is it's combined exo and endo skeleton. The main torso's skeletal parts largely resemble those of a flying fox apart from the extra bones in the front part of the torso, which support the two extra arms. Apart from the head, hind legs and torso, all other bones reside outside the body as Isopod-like exo skeleton.

name: Brain of Tiger Shark
description:
Belonging to the order Carcharhiniformes (ground sharks) and the family Galeocerdonidae (tiger sharks), Galeocerdo cuvier (Péron & Lesueur, 1822) is a large, solitary predator found in tropical and subtropical waters, especially around islands and coastal areas. It gets its name from the dark vertical stripes on its body, resembling a tiger’s pattern. This fish is an opportunistic carnivore, consuming a wide range of prey, earning it the nickname “garbage can of the sea” and they can reach up to 7.5 meters in length and weigh over 3,000 kg. Despite its ecological importance, the tiger shark faces significant threats from overfishing, habitat loss, and the shark fin trade.

This 3D model is part of a project that aims to compare the structure of the brains of different vertebrate groups and, therefore, facilitate the study of their neuroanatomy.

name: Equine Atlas C1 — Veterinary Anatomy 3D Model
description:
3D model of an equine atlas vertebra, also known as the first cervical vertebra (C1), developed from a real anatomical specimen for educational use in Veterinary Anatomy. The atlas is located between the skull and the axis and is relevant for the study of the cervical spine, osteology, vertebral morphology, and the atlanto-occipital region in horses.

This model was prepared for digital visualization and may be used as a complementary teaching resource in practical anatomy classes. It can also support 3D printing workflows, depending on the final mesh preparation and slicing parameters. For physical reproduction, FDM 3D printing with PLA filament is recommended, with print orientation, supports, and infill adjusted according to the slicing software.

This model is part of a project focused on the development and dissemination of 3D animal bone models to support practical teaching in Veterinary Anatomy at IF Goiano — Campus Urutaí.

Tyrannosaurus rex is the type species of the genus Tyrannosaurus, a member of the family Tyrannosaurids. It was one of the largest land predators in Earth's history.

Time and Habitat
Tyrannosaurus rex lived during the late Cretaceous Period, approximately 67–66 million years ago. It inhabited what is now western North America, which at that time was an island continent called Laramidia.

Anatomical Features
Like other members of its family, Tyrannosaurus was a bipedal predator with a massive skull balanced by a long, heavy, and stiff tail.

name: Yellow Guppy Male
description:
Yellow Guppy Male. The yellow guppy will always have a yellow tail. This may range from the palest to the deepest, almost orange, yellow color.
However, the body coloring may vary depending on the tail style. Yellow coloration appears on the gills and fins, but this color can appear in many other places as well; yellow splashes are seen on the fish’s face when it opens its mouth to eat a piece of food. Another characteristic feature these fishes have is extra flaps that catch more sunlight than if those parts were barely allowing them better access to what little light there is.

If you decide to get one for your tank, these fish are known for being very active swimmers that love bright lights and have an aggressive temperament so do not house them together unless you want your guppy in trouble! They like doing well on any type of food, whether it is fruits or pellets.

name: Lobo Ancião — SkyZRP
description:
O Lobo Ancião é um predador experiente e resistente às regiões selvagens de Skyrim, marcado por anos de sobrevivência em ambientes hostis. Seu corpo apresenta sinais claros de idade e dos consideráveis confrontos que ocorreram ao longo de sua vida, mas sua experiência o tornou ainda mais perigosa.

A criatura foi desenvolvida como um recurso de fauna fantástico para o projeto de Skyrim roleplay SkyZRP, combinando a anatomia realista de um lobo com características de uma criatura veterana das regiões selvagens de Skyrim.

Tipo: Grande Predador

Habitat: Montanhas, florestas densas e regiões nevadas

Tamanho: 1,10–1,30 m no ombro

Comprimento total: 2,30–2,80 m incluindo a cauda

Peso: 90–140 kg

Estilo: fantasia realista do norte

They are typically found in larger groups and will eat just about anything they can sink their teeth into. If you spot one, seek professional aid immedaitely, they are not dangerous alone but where there is one there’s always more and they are some of the hardest of pests to get rid of.

name: Somatolactin (Sl)
description:
Sl-producing cells are mainly found in the pars intermedia (PI), adjacent to the neurohypophysis. In teleosts, somatolactin has been associated with metabolism, acid-base balance, and reproductive physiology. In this model, Sl cells are shown in yellow.

How to interact: rotate by dragging, zoom with the mouse wheel, and click on the annotations to explore specific anatomical regions and hormonal cell populations.

Methods (summary): anatomical segmentation was guided by histology and immunohistochemistry for Prl, Gh, Acth/Pomc, Tsh, Fsh, Lh, Sl, and α-Msh. The 3D reconstruction was developed in Blender and exported in glTF format for web visualization.

name: Coyote
description:
The coyote,is a species of canine also known as the American jackal,It is native to North America, and it is smaller than its close relative, the gray wolf, and slightly smaller than the closely related eastern wolf and red wolf. It fills much of the same ecological niche as the golden jackal does in Eurasia but the coyote is generally larger.

The coyote is listed as least concern by the International Union for Conservation of Nature, due to its wide distribution and abundance throughout North America. The species is versatile, able to adapt to and expand into environments modified by humans.
Humans are the coyote's greatest threat, followed by cougars and gray wolves.

name: Graptolite - Didymograptus sp.
description:
**Nom** : *Didymograptus sp.*.

**Description** : Les graptolites appartiennent à l’embranchement des Hémichordés, à la classe des Graptolithacés. Ils vivent en colonies (rhabdosome) constituées à partir d’un individu initial appelé sicule. Un stolon chitinisé constitue l’axe central de la colonie et possède un nombre variable de branches, les stipes. Le stolon comporte une série de thèques, petite loge latérale, où vivent les individus composant la colonie. Chez *Didymograptus*, les thèques disposées sur un axe double.

**Dimensions** : 21,7 cm x 13,2 cm x 1,2 cm.

**Répartition stratigraphique** : Ordovicien.

**Âge** : Ordovicien.

**Localité** : inconnue.

**Méthode** : Acquisition de 572 photos avec Appareil Reflexe APS-C dans Studio Photos. Modèle reconstruit par photogrammétrie avec le logiciel Agisoft Metashape.

name: Brain of Great Freshwater Stingray
description:
*Potamotrygon rex* Carvalho, 2016 is a freshwater stingray endemic to the Amazon basin, standing out for its unique dorsal pattern, consisting of light-colored spots and rosettes on a dark background, which distinguishes it from other freshwater stingrays. Like other members of its genus,*Potamotrygon rex* has a venomous tail spine used for defense. This benthic fish is associated with sandy bottoms and has a predominantly entomophagous diet, feeding mainly on insects, both adults and larvae. Additionally, it also includes fish, mollusks, and crustaceans in its diet.

This 3D model is part of a project that aims to compare the structure of the brains of different vertebrate groups and, therefore, facilitate the study of their neuroanatomy.

It is classified as vulnerable.

Eagle is the common name for certain large birds of prey within the family of the Accipitridae. While on a genetic level, only the subfamily Aquilinae comprises "true eagles", many other species are commonly referred to as eagles, such as the bald eagle, and the term generally carries no taxonomic weight. Most of the 68 species of eagles are from Eurasia and Africa.[1] Outside this area, just 14 species can be found—two in North America, nine in Central and South America, and three in Australia.

Eagles are not a natural group but denote essentially any kind of bird of prey large enough to hunt sizeable (about 50 cm long or more overall) vertebrates.

name: Minecraft gray whale
description: From wikipedia: The gray whale (Eschrichtius robustus),[1] also known as the grey whale,[6] is a baleen whale that migrates between feeding and breeding grounds yearly. It reaches a length of 14.9–15.2 m (49–50 ft), a weight of up to 41 to 45 tonnes (45 to 50 short tons; 40 to 44 long tons) and lives between 55 and 70 years, although one female was estimated to be 75–80 years of age.[7][8][9][10] One of the longest-living gray whales currently is a female, first sighted in 1977, and estimated to be 53–55 years old as of 2024.[11] The common name of the whale comes from the gray patches and white mottling on its dark skin.[12] Gray whales were once called devil fish because of their fighting behavior when hunted.[13] The gray whale is the sole living species in the genus Eschrichtius. It is the sole living genus in the family Eschrichtiidae; however, some recent studies classify it as a member of the family Balaenopteridae. This mammal is descended from filter-feeding whales that appeared during the Neogene.

name: Ecuadorian White-fronted Capuchin
description:
Quad mesh, 6001 vertices, Basecolor, roughness, normal map, 30 fps animation, 58 frames, Made in Blender and Substance Painter.


Cebus aequatorialis

This primate is considered a subspecies of Cebus albifrons and is distinguished by more vivid coloration in its fur, as well as a more robust body. 

It is a diurnal species, highly active and intelligent. Its ecological role includes seed dispersal and the control of insect populations.

It is currently classified as Critically Endangered due to the ongoing loss of vegetation cover within its range.

Other threats it faces include commercial hunting, retaliation by farmers who consider it a pest to corn crops, and the illegal pet trade.

In addition to thousands of snail and mussel shells, the collection also contains approximately 200 art and everyday objects as well as ethnographic objects. name: Bovine Tibia  (Bos taurus)
description:
High-resolution 3D anatomical scan of an isolated Bovine Tibia (Bos taurus).

This digital model provides a highly accurate and detailed representation of the distal hindlimb osteology in large ruminants. The scan  illustrates key diagnostic features of the bovine tibia, including the wide proximal extremity with its medial and lateral condyles, the prominent intercondylar eminence (eminentia intercondylaris), the sharp tibial cranial crest (crista tibiae), and the distal cochlea for the tarsal articulation. It serves as an essential digital resource for veterinary students, morphologists.

Source / Provenance: This specimen is part of the anatomical collection curated by Professor Antonio Palladino, Professor of Veterinary Anatomy, Histology, and Embryology at the University of Rome Tor Vergata.

Suggested Use: Educational purposes, veterinary research, comparative anatomy study, and scientific visualization.

Cada entalhe homenageia aqueles que enfrentaram a adversidade. A obra destaca a urgência de politicas públicas que garantam a melhoria das condições de vida da população brasileira e faz um apelo à preservação da natureza em nosso pais.

name: Estatua de león de piedra
description:
Modelo 3D fotogramétrico de una estatua de león de piedra
·
Esta estatua se encuentra en el "Jardín del Partenón" del Hotel Convento I, en la localidad de Coreses, provincia de Zamora.
·
El edificio que da nombre a este jardín recuerda a los antiguos templos clásicos de Grecia.
·
El actual Hotel Convento I fue, en sus orígenes, un antiguo seminario de la Orden alemana "Misioneros del Verbo Divino", que iniciaron su obra en España para tratar de paliar las consecuencias de la Guerra Civil. Así inauguraron la localidad de Coreses (Zamora) en junio de 1949.
·
Para la construcción del edificio hotelero se emplearon materiales originales, como la piedra, que fue recuperada de las ruinas de una ermita románica. Los ladrillos provienen de Ávila, donde se fabrican según el antiguo estilo mudéjar. La madera perteneció a viejas casonas nobles y a palacios ya desaparecidos.
·
Puedes adquirir este modelo 3D en mi perfil de Fab: https://www.fab.com/sellers/Kalathos

name: Equine Humerus — Veterinary 3D Model
description:
3D model of the equine humerus, developed from a real anatomical specimen for educational use in Veterinary Anatomy. The humerus is a long bone of the thoracic limb, located between the scapula and the radius-ulna region, and is important for the study of osteology, limb morphology, and locomotor anatomy in horses.

This model was prepared for digital visualization and may support 3D printing workflows. For physical reproduction, FDM printing with PLA is recommended, with orientation, supports, and infill adjusted in the slicer.

name: Phyllomedusa chaparroi - MNCN2682
description:
**Description**: This 3D model features Chaparro’s monkey frog, an amphibian species endemic to central Peru. As a paratype, it serves as a critical reference for the scientific description of the species. The visualization highlights the specialized morphology of this "monkey frog," famous for its ability to produce waxy lipid secretions. By rubbing these fats over its body, the frog creates a waterproof barrier that minimizes evaporative water loss, a fascinating adaptation to arboreal lifestyle.

**Specimen**: *Phyllomedusa chaparroi* (Castroviejo-Fisher, Köhler, De la Riva, Padial, 2017).

**Inventory number**: MNCN-2682

**Collection**: Museo Nacional de Ciencias Naturales, Herpetology. Curator: Marta Calvo (mcalvo@mncn.csic.es).

**More about**:

Find more about the MNCN [here](http:mncn.csic.es/en).

Find more about the collection [here](http:mncn.csic.es/es/colecciones/cientificas/herpetologia).

Scanned with an Artec Spider in 2026 by Leticia Herrera and Carlos A. Palancar.

description: Modeled from images of a real specimen. The Rodrigues Solitaire (Pezophaps solitaria) was a large, flightless bird endemic to Rodrigues Island in the Indian Ocean and a close relative of the dodo. It was driven to extinction in the 18th century due to overhunting by humans and the introduction of invasive species that preyed on eggs and altered its habitat. Early accounts describe its territorial behavior and distinctive wing knobs used in combat. Base model created with AI tools, then sculpted/edited in Blender for scientific accuracy.

name: Bird on the Rocks
description:
A small stylized environment study focused on hand-painted rock materials with soft watercolor-inspired texture work. Even though the scene is minimal, I approached it with the same attention to shape language, material readability, and color composition that I would apply to a larger production asset.
The rocks were built from simple sculpted forms to achieve stronger silhouettes and more natural surface flow, while the final look relies heavily on hand-painted textures and controlled value work. I wanted the materials to feel painterly and stylized without losing structure or depth.
One of my favorite details is the small robin perched among the grey mossy stones, adding a bright focal point and a subtle sense of life and scale to the composition.

Projects like this are a great way to explore stylized workflows, refine brush economy, and experiment with how far atmosphere and storytelling can be pushed through relatively simple assets.

Original concept art by Arthur Bourgeais.
